newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee touches six-month peak vs forward dlr.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee touches six-month peak vs forward dlr.

text.p: The Indian rupee continued to extend gains, touching a six-month peak in the forward dollar market on Monday on the back of easing domestic money market conditions, dealers said.
Premia on six-month dollar opened at 1.13/1.16 rupees on Monday, down from the weekend closing of 1.17/1.19 rupees.
Dealers said the annualised six-month premia, at 5.75 percent, was the lowest in the last six months.
Some companies expect call rates to fall further. "I expect six-month premium to fall to a low of 85/95 paise," said Yeshwant Rao, deputy general manager (Forex) at Arvind Mills.
The falling premia had nothing to with activities of Indian exporters and importers, a Bombay bank dealer said.
He said it was a function of banks' need to swap their expatriate Indians' dollar accounts to generate rupees for onlending to local clients.
He said the falling premia reflected the falling call money rates. Last week, call money rates touched a low of 2.0-3.0 percent. Call rates were quoted at 2.0-2.25 percent on Monday.
Dealers said Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) permission to banks to lend out their expatriate Indian dollar deposits had not yet impacted the forward dollar market.
"Except that some banks may be reducing their rollover (swapping of expatriate dollars into rupees) as they are looking to lend in dollars," said a dealer.
Last month, RBI allowed banks to lend out their FCNR (foreign currency non-resident) dollar account to local firms.

"The six-month swapped funds will cost about 13.25 percent for local firms (5.5 percent interest payable to expatriate Indian plus 5.75 percent forward premia plus two percent spread)," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Bombay.
He said this would be cheaper than State Bank of India's prime lending rate of 14.5 percent.
